mainTopic: Breaking שבת to testify about the new moon, the meaning of בעליל, and whether anyone matched משה
overview: The משנה teaches that today, witnesses who saw the new moon may break שבת to testify only for ניסן and תשרי. When the בית המקדש stood, they did so every month because of the ראש חודש קרבן. The גמרא resolves a contradiction with an earlier משנה that speaks of six months: אביי explains that for ניסן and תשרי the messengers wait until בית דין declares 'מקודש', and a ברייתא supports him. A ברייתא then learns from a פסוק that שבת may be broken to declare the month, but not so that people can keep the festivals. Another ברייתא tells how רבן יוחנן בן זכאי limited the practice to ניסן and תשרי after the destruction. A new משנה debates whether witnesses break שבת when the moon was seen clearly (בעליל), and tells of רבן גמליאל warning רבי עקיבא not to hold witnesses back. The גמרא proves the meaning of עליל from a פסוק in תהלים. That פסוק leads to רב and שמואל's teaching about the fifty gates of understanding and whether שלמה could match משה.

steps.title: Witnesses may break שבת for two months
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that witnesses may break שבת to testify about the new moon only for ניסן and תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: For two months witnesses may break שבת: ניסן and תשרי. In these months messengers go out to סוריא, and these months set the dates of the יום טובים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a rule: witnesses who saw the new moon may break שבת to travel and testify, but only for ניסן and תשרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two reasons are given. Messengers are sent out in these months, and the big יום טובים (פסח in ניסן; ראש השנה, יום כיפור and סוכות in תשרי) depend on getting the date right. That is important enough to override שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Messengers sent out to tell far-away Jews the date
Syria, the land just outside ארץ ישראל
They set the dates of the יום טובים correctly

steps.whyThisMatters: The phrase 'שבהן שלוחין יוצאין' sounds like messengers go out only in these two months. That reading sets up the גמרא's question in step 3.

phrases.english: MISHNA: For two months
they may desecrate Shabbat:
phrases.notes: He means the witnesses who saw the new moon, travelling on שבת to testify.

phrases.english: for Nisan and for Tishrei,
for in them messengers go out to Syria,
and by them the Festivals are set.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ עַל שְׁנֵי חֳדָשִׁים מְחַלְּלִין אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses may break שבת to testify about the new moon only for ניסן and תשרי, because messengers go out then and the יום טובים depend on them.

steps.title: In Temple times, שבת was broken for every month
steps.stepSummary: When the בית המקדש stood, witnesses broke שבת for every month so the ראש חודש קרבן would be brought on time.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the בית המקדש was standing, they broke שבת for all the months, because of setting the קרבן properly.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds that the two-month limit applies only today. When the בית המקדש stood, witnesses broke שבת for every month.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every ראש חודש had its own קרבן, which had to be brought on the correct day. Getting the date right therefore mattered every month, not only for the יום טוב months.

keyTerms.meaning: All of them, meaning all the months
Setting the קרבן properly, so it is brought on the right day

steps.whatToRemember: Today: break שבת only for ניסן and תשרי. When the בית המקדש stood: break שבת for every month, because of the ראש חודש קרבן.

phrases.english: And when the Temple was standing,
they would desecrate Shabbat even for all of them,
because of the proper setting of the offering.
phrases.notes: This is the special קרבן brought on every ראש חודש.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Part of the same משנה as step 1
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits step 1's two-month rule to the time after the בית המקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the בית המקדש stood, witnesses broke שבת for all months because of the ראש חודש קרבן.

steps.title: Only two months? Another משנה says six
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges our משנה with an earlier משנה, which says messengers go out for six months, not two.
steps.simpleTranslation: Only for two months and no more? Here is a contradiction: an earlier משנה says messengers go out for six months!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads our משנה as saying messengers go out only in ניסן and תשרי. It then quotes an earlier משנה that says they go out for six months.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה gives 'שבהן שלוחין יוצאין' as the special reason for these two months. That suggests messengers go out only for them. The earlier משנה lists six months with messengers, so the two sources seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: And they set them against each other: a contradiction between two sources

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about breaking שבת. It is about the משנה's reason: our משנה seems to say messengers go out only in two months, while the other משנה says six.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ עַל שְׁנֵי חֳדָשִׁים וְתוּ לָא?!
phrases.english: GEMARA: For two months and no more?!
And raise a contradiction:
For six months the messengers go out!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how step 1 should be read.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that messengers go out in ניסן and תשרי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If messengers go out for six months, they are not unique to ניסן and תשרי, so this cannot be what makes those two months special.

steps.title: אביי: in ניסן and תשרי the messengers wait for the declaration
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that messengers go out in all six months. For ניסן and תשרי, however, they wait until בית דין says 'מקודש'.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: this is what the משנה means. For all the other months, messengers leave the night before. For ניסן and תשרי, they do not leave until they hear בית דין say 'מקודש'.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the contradiction by explaining what the משנה really means. The difference is not whether messengers go out, but when they leave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the other months, messengers can leave the evening before, once it is clear the day will be ראש חודש. For ניסן and תשרי, the יום טובים depend on the date, so they wait for בית דין's formal declaration 'מקודש', which happens only by day. So both משניות are true: messengers go out for six months, and ניסן and תשרי are special because of this waiting.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (a rereading of the source)
From the evening, the night before
The court that declares ראש חודש
'It is sanctified', the formal declaration of ראש חודש

steps.whatToRemember: Messengers go out for six months. Only for ניסן and תשרי do they wait to hear בית דין say 'מקודש' before leaving.

phrases.english: Abaye said: This is what it is saying:
For all of them, messengers go out from the evening;
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means the other months that have messengers.

phrases.english: for Nisan and for Tishrei,
phrases.notes: The words 'they do not go out' are left unsaid but assumed here.

phrases.english: not until they hear from the mouth of the court: 'Sanctified.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה (הכי קאמר): the special point is the timing of the messengers, not whether they go out.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say messengers go out only for ניסן and תשרי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Messengers go out for six months. For ניסן and תשרי they wait for בית דין's declaration of 'מקודש'.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports אביי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches exactly what אביי said.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: for all the months, messengers leave the night before. For ניסן and תשרי, they wait until they hear בית דין say 'מקודש'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as אביי, which confirms his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא matches אביי's words almost exactly. This shows his explanation is an older teaching, not something he made up to fix the contradiction. That settles the question.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way: a ברייתא that supports the previous statement

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא confirms אביי: ניסן and תשרי are special because the messengers wait for 'מקודש'.

phrases.english: It is also taught so in a baraita:
For all of them they go out from the evening;
for Nisan and for Tishrei,
not until they hear from the mouth of the court: 'Sanctified.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's answer in step 4.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same wording

steps.title: Where do we learn that witnesses may break שבת?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks for the source that allows breaking שבת for the new moon.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: How do we know that witnesses may break שבת to testify about the new months?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that asks for the source of the rule. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה said witnesses break שבת, but it did not say how we know this. Breaking שבת is very serious, so the ברייתא wants a פסוק that allows it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught (this opens a ברייתא)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
From where do we know that one may desecrate
Shabbat for them?
phrases.notes: "Them" means the new months. The witnesses travel on שבת to report that they saw the new moon.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִנַּיִן שֶׁמְּחַלְּלִין עֲלֵיהֶן אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the contradiction between the two משניות, the גמרא now looks for the פסוק behind the rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source that allows witnesses to break שבת for the new moon.

steps.title: The verse about declaring the festivals in their time
steps.stepSummary: The source is the פסוק that says the festivals must be declared in their proper time.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'These are the festivals of ה׳ which you shall declare in their set times.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בְּמוֹעֲדָם' (in their set time) shows that the timing of the festivals is very important. That timing depends on declaring ראש חודש on the right day, so the witnesses may break שבת for it.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"These are the festivals of ה׳
which you shall declare in their set times."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:4

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: אֵלֶּה מוֹעֲדֵי ה׳ אֲשֶׁר תִּקְרְאוּ אוֹתָם בְּמוֹעֲדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'אשר תקראו אותם במועדם' shows that the festivals must be set on time, and this allows breaking שבת.

steps.title: Maybe שבת may also be broken so the festivals are kept
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests a wider rule: perhaps one may also break שבת so that people keep the festivals on the correct day.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think: just as we break שבת so the months get declared, we should also break שבת so the festivals are kept on the right day.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible mistake, using the word 'יכול' (you might think). This sets up the limit that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two separate things depend on the new moon. First, בית דין has to declare it. Second, messengers have to tell everyone so they keep the festivals on the right day. The ברייתא asks whether the permission to break שבת covers the messengers too.

keyTerms.meaning: You might think (a mistaken idea that the ברייתא will reject)
That they become sanctified (declared by בית דין)
That they are kept (observed by the people)

steps.confusionAlert: 'יכול' does not state the הלכה. It introduces an idea that the ברייתא is about to reject.

phrases.english: One might think that just as we desecrate Shabbat
so that they become sanctified,
so too we desecrate Shabbat so that they are kept —
phrases.notes: This means the messengers who travel to tell people which day was declared, so they keep the festivals on the right day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests how far the permission learned in step 7 should reach.
steps.kashyaTarget: The scope of the permission learned from 'במועדם'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If keeping the festivals on time is the goal, then informing the people should also be allowed on שבת, not only declaring the month.

steps.title: שבת may be broken for declaring, not for observing
steps.stepSummary: The words 'אשר תקראו אותם' limit the permission to the declaration of the month.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'which you shall declare them.' This teaches that you may break שבת for declaring the month, but not for its observance.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the wider idea by pointing to the exact words of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק stresses 'declaring' (קריאה), which is the job of בית דין and its witnesses. Telling people afterward is about 'keeping' (קיום), so that does not override שבת. So the witnesses who come to testify may travel on שבת, but the messengers who carry the news may not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why witnesses may travel on שבת but the messengers who spread the news may not.

phrases.english: The verse says: "which you shall declare them,"
for their declaration you may desecrate Shabbat,
but you may not desecrate Shabbat for their observance.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: אֲשֶׁר תִּקְרְאוּ אוֹתָם, עַל קְרִיאָתָם אַתָּה מְחַלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the suggestion of step 8 by limiting the permission.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the פסוק narrows the scope of the rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Breaking שבת is allowed both for declaring the month and for keeping the festivals.
steps.terutzMaskana: Breaking שבת is allowed only for the declaration (קריאה), not for the observance (קיום).

steps.title: Back to the משנה: in Temple times they broke שבת for every month
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about the בית המקדש and brings a ברייתא confirming that at first they broke שבת for all months.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: when the בית המקדש stood, they broke שבת for all the months because of the קרבן. The Rabbis taught: at first, they would break שבת for all the months.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and brings a ברייתא about it. This sets up the story of what changed in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ראש חודש קרבן had to be brought on the correct day each month. So every month's declaration mattered, not just ניסן and תשרי. The ברייתא calls this the original practice, which hints that it later changed.

keyTerms.meaning: Setting the offering right (so it is brought on time)

phrases.english: And when the Temple was standing,
they would desecrate Shabbat even for all of them,
because of setting the offering right.
The Rabbis taught: At first
they would desecrate Shabbat even for all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֶׁהָיָה בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים מְחַלְּלִין אַף עַל כּוּלָּן מִפְּנֵי תַּקָּנַת הַקׇּרְבָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the source of the rule to the משנה's line about Temple times (step 2).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the time of the בית המקדש, witnesses broke שבת for every month because of the ראש חודש קרבן.

steps.title: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי limits it to ניסן and תשרי
steps.stepSummary: After the destruction, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי ruled that there is no longer a קרבן, so שבת is broken only for ניסן and תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: After the בית המקדש was destroyed, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי said: Is there a קרבן now? They decided that שבת would be broken only for ניסן and תשרי.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells how and why the practice changed after the destruction. This explains the rule at the start of our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for breaking שבת every month was the קרבן. Once there was no קרבן, that reason was gone. What remained was ניסן and תשרי, which set the dates of the major festivals.

keyTerms.meaning: The leading sage at the time of the destruction

steps.whatToRemember: Witnesses break שבת to declare the month (קריאה), not for its observance. In Temple times this applied to every month because of the קרבן. After the destruction, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי limited it to ניסן and תשרי.

phrases.english: Once the Temple was destroyed,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי:
phrases.english: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai said to them:
Is there an offering?
phrases.notes: He is asking this to make a point: there is no קרבן anymore, so the reason for breaking שבת every month is gone.

phrases.english: They established that they should not desecrate Shabbat

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עַל נִיסָן וְעַל תִּשְׁרִי בִּלְבַד.
phrases.english: except for Nisan and Tishrei alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשֶּׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, אָמַר לָהֶן רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the history begun in step 10 and explains the משנה's rule in step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Without a קרבן, breaking שבת is limited to ניסן and תשרי, as decided by רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.

steps.title: New משנה: שבת is broken whether or not the moon was clearly seen
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that witnesses break שבת even if the moon was clearly visible to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Whether the moon was seen clearly or was not seen clearly, the witnesses may break שבת to testify about it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It asks whether it matters if the moon was easy for everyone to see.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One could think that if everyone saw the moon clearly, these witnesses are not really needed. The first opinion says they still go and break שבת either way.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Whether it was seen clearly,
phrases.notes: "It" is the new moon. "בעליל" means so clearly that everyone could see it.

phrases.english: or whether it was not seen clearly,
one may desecrate Shabbat for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּין שֶׁנִּרְאָה בַּעֲלִיל, בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא נִרְאָה בַּעֲלִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, moving on from the previous topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses break שבת for the new moon whether or not it was clearly visible.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: if clearly seen, שבת is not broken
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי disagrees and says that if the moon was clearly visible, the witnesses may not break שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: If the moon was seen clearly, they may not break שבת for it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי gives a different opinion from the first part of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי makes the clear-sighting case different. The משנה does not give his reason. The simple idea is that when everyone can see the moon, others will surely testify, so these witnesses do not need to break שבת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
If it was seen clearly,
they may not desecrate Shabbat for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אִם נִרְאָה בַּעֲלִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion in step 12 about a clearly seen moon.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, if the moon was clearly visible, witnesses do not break שבת.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא holds back the witnesses, and רבן גמליאל objects
steps.stepSummary: The משנה tells a story. רבי עקיבא stopped more than forty pairs of witnesses in לוד from traveling on שבת. רבן גמליאל warned him that this would make witnesses stop coming in the future.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once, more than forty pairs of witnesses were traveling, and רבי עקיבא held them back in לוד. רבן גמליאל sent him a message: If you hold back the public, you will cause them to stumble in the future.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a story about a real case of witnesses traveling on שבת to report the new moon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא thought there was no need for so many witnesses to break שבת. רבן גמליאל disagreed, because witnesses who are turned away may not bother to come next time, when they are really needed. The story backs up the first opinion, that witnesses go even when many others have already seen the moon.

keyTerms.meaning: A pair (here, a pair of witnesses)
He held them back / detained them
A town on the way to ירושלים

steps.whatToRemember: רבן גמליאל's concern is for the future. If witnesses are turned away now, they may not come later when the בית דין truly needs them.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a rule can protect a system as a whole. Sometimes we allow something that looks unnecessary right now so that the system keeps working.

phrases.english: There was an incident where more than forty pairs passed through
phrases.notes: These are pairs of witnesses on their way to ירושלים to report seeing the new moon.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Akiva held them back in Lod
Rabban Gamliel sent him a message:
If you hold back the many people,
you will end up making them stumble in the future.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the משנה with a story that supports the first opinion (step 12) over רבי יוסי (step 13).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses should not be held back from breaking שבת to testify, because turning them away would discourage them in the future.

steps.title: How do we know עליל means clearly visible?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins and asks for the source showing that the word עליל, used in the משנה, means 'revealed' or 'clearly visible.'
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: How do we know that this word עליל means 'revealed'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts by asking about a word in the משנה. It wants proof that עליל means 'clearly seen.' This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה used the phrase 'נראה בעליל' (steps 12 and 13). Because עליל is an unusual word, the גמרא wants a source for its meaning.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
From where is it understood that this word "alil"
is a term meaning "revealed"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע דְּהַאי עֲלִיל לִישָּׁנָא דְּמִיגַּלֵּי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה to the גמרא, asking about a word the משנה used.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that עליל means 'clearly visible.'

steps.title: רבי אבהו proves the meaning from a verse in תהלים
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו quotes a פסוק where 'בעליל לארץ' means silver refined in full view of the world. This shows that עליל means clearly visible.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: The פסוק says, 'The words of ה׳ are pure words, silver refined in clear view of the earth, purified seven times.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the question by bringing a פסוק that uses the same word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, 'בעליל לארץ' describes something done openly, in front of the whole world. So in the משנה, 'נראה בעליל' means the moon was seen clearly and openly.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
The verse says:
"The words of ה׳ are pure words,
phrases.notes: תהלים 12:7

phrases.english: silver refined in clear view of the earth,
purified seven times."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in תהלים uses 'בעליל לארץ' to mean openly, before the world, so עליל means clearly visible.

steps.title: Fifty gates of understanding, and משה received all but one
steps.stepSummary: Going off on a side topic from the same פסוק, one of רב and שמואל teaches that fifty gates of understanding were created. משה received forty-nine of them, as the פסוק says, 'You made him a little less than God.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל: One said, fifty gates of understanding were created in the world, and all were given to משה except one, as it says, 'And You made him a little less than God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the topic of the moon and brings a teaching connected to the words 'purified seven times' in the פסוק just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Seven times' is read as seven times seven, which is forty-nine. Since fifty gates exist, משה lacked only one. The פסוק 'a little less than God' supports the idea that man reaches almost, but not quite, the highest level.

keyTerms.meaning: And You made him a little less than God

steps.confusionAlert: Only one opinion of רב and שמואל appears here. The other one's view comes in step 19, so do not assume they agree.

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel [disagree]:
phrases.notes: This builds on 'purified seven times' from the פסוק just quoted: seven times seven, which is forty-nine.

phrases.english: One said:
Fifty gates of understanding were created in the world,
and all of them were given to Moshe
except for one,
as it says: "And You made him a little less than God."
phrases.notes: תהלים 8:6

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same פסוק from step 16 to start a side teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are fifty gates of understanding, and משה received forty-nine of them.

steps.title: קהלת wanted to equal משה, and a heavenly voice said no
steps.stepSummary: קהלת (שלמה) wanted to reach משה's level. A בת קול told him that no prophet would ever arise in ישראל like משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'קהלת sought to find words of delight': קהלת wanted to be like משה. A בת קול came out and told him: 'And what is written uprightly, words of truth,' meaning the תורה, which says: 'No prophet ever arose again in ישראל like משה.'
steps.whatsHappening: Continuing the same opinion, the גמרא shows from a פסוק in קהלת that שלמה tried to reach משה's level and was told it could not be done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Words of delight' is read as שלמה's attempt to reach the level of משה. The בת קול points him to the 'words of truth,' the תורה, where it says no prophet would be like משה.
steps.whatToRemember: משה's level of understanding is unique. Even שלמה, the wisest king, could not reach it.

phrases.english: "Kohelet sought to find words of delight":
phrases.notes: קהלת 12:10

phrases.english: Kohelet wanted to be like Moshe.
A heavenly voice came out and said to him:
"And what was written uprightly, words of truth":
phrases.notes: The rest of the same פסוק. The 'words of truth' are the תורה, and the next line shows what it says.

phrases.english: "And no prophet arose again in Israel like Moshe."
phrases.notes: דברים 34:10

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the first opinion from step 17 by showing that no one after משה could reach his level.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שלמה tried to reach משה's level, and a בת קול told him that no prophet would be like משה.

steps.title: No prophet like משה arose, but a king did
steps.stepSummary: The other of רב and שמואל reads the פסוק narrowly: no prophet arose like משה, but among kings one did arise.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one said: Among the prophets, no one like משה arose. Among the kings, one did arise.
steps.whatsHappening: Now we hear the second opinion from the pair רב and שמואל. He says the פסוק only rules out a PROPHET like משה, so a KING, שלמה, could still match him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 used 'ולא קם נביא עוד בישראל כמשה' to show that שלמה failed to reach משה's level. This opinion focuses on the word נביא: the פסוק limits only prophets, so שלמה, as a king, could be equal to משה in wisdom. This sets up a problem with the פסוק 'בקש קהלת' that the first opinion had explained.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one said, introducing the second opinion of the pair

steps.confusionAlert: This opinion does not say any prophet matched משה. It agrees no prophet did. It only says a king, שלמה, could reach his level.

phrases.english: And one said: among the prophets, none arose like him,
among the kings, one did arise.
phrases.notes: He means שלמה, a king whose wisdom matched משה's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second opinion of רב and שמואל, which reads the פסוק quoted in step 18 differently.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק 'no prophet arose like משה' refers only to prophets. Among kings, שלמה did reach משה's level.

steps.title: Then what was קהלת seeking?
steps.stepSummary: If שלמה did reach משה's level, how do we explain the פסוק 'קהלת sought to find words of delight'?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then how do I explain the פסוק 'קהלת sought to find words of delight'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question on this second opinion. It sets up the next step, which gives a new explanation of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion read 'בקש קהלת' as שלמה trying, and failing, to reach משה's level. If שלמה did reach that level, then 'sought' cannot mean that, because you don't 'seek' something you already have. So the פסוק needs a new explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: But then how do I explain (literally 'uphold') this פסוק?
The name שלמה uses for himself in ספר קהלת

phrases.english: But how do I uphold
'קהלת sought to find words of delight'?
phrases.notes: קהלת 12:10

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the פסוק of קהלת means according to the opinion in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: According to the opinion that שלמה did match משה, what did קהלת 'seek' and fail to get?

steps.title: קהלת wanted to judge without witnesses
steps.stepSummary: שלמה wanted to judge cases by reading people's hearts, without witnesses or warning. A בת קול answered with the rest of his own פסוק, pointing to the rule of two witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: קהלת wanted to judge cases based on what is in the heart, without witnesses and without warning. A בת קול came out and said to him: 'And written uprightly, words of truth,' meaning: 'By the mouth of two witnesses' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: what שלמה 'sought' was the power to judge people by seeing into their hearts. A בת קול told him no, the תורה says a court acts only through two witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With his great wisdom, שלמה thought he could know who was guilty without the usual process of עדים and התראה. The בת קול answers with the second half of the same פסוק, 'וכתוב יושר דברי אמת', and explains that the 'written words of truth' are the תורה's rule of two witnesses. So even the wisest judge must follow the written law, not his own sense of who is guilty.

keyTerms.meaning: Judgments based on what is in the heart, judging by inner knowledge alone
A warning given to someone before he sins, which a court needs before it can punish
And so on: the פסוק continues

steps.whatToRemember: According to this opinion, שלמה matched משה, but he still could not judge without witnesses and warning. The תורה's rule of two witnesses binds even the wisest judge.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a court follows the תורה's set process of witnesses and warning, even when the judge believes he knows the truth some other way.

phrases.english: קהלת sought to judge judgments of the heart,
without witnesses and without warning.
A heavenly voice came out and said to him:
'And written uprightly, words of truth',
phrases.notes: This is the second half of the same פסוק, קהלת 12:10.

phrases.english: 'By the mouth of two witnesses,' and so on.
phrases.notes: דברים 17:6. The בת קול is pointing to this as the 'written words of truth.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20 by giving a new meaning to 'בקש קהלת'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קהלת sought to judge by reading hearts, without witnesses or warning. The בת קול rejected this with 'וכתוב יושר דברי אמת', which refers to the rule of two witnesses.
